result.title: Reconstruction-Based Diagnosis through Gödel-Regularized Virtual Observability
result.summary: Not every component in a technical system can be equipped with sensors. Hence, when a fault occurs, available sensors often detect it only after its effects have propagated. This makes the isolation of faults difficult. We approach this problem by introducing virtual sensors. For each combination of component and fault type, we let external knowledge describe the fault-sensitive variables. We introduce a novel neural observer that is only trained on normal data. For fault isolation, it uses available sensor measurements where it is possible and reconstructs missing variables as virtual sensors to predict normal behavior. It detects deviations between current values and nominal predictions and computes local symptoms, which are then compared by onset time. The result is a set of root causes describing the faulty behavior. We use Gödel logic to encode physical knowledge and guide training. We evaluate our approach on synthetic networks, the Tennessee Eastman Process, and datasets of two modular production plants.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向传感器覆盖不全的技术系统，提出仅用正常数据训练的神经网络观测器：借助外部知识指定各「部件-故障类型」的敏感变量，在可测处使用真实传感值、在缺失处重建为虚拟传感器，再按局部症状的起始时间比较来定位根因，并以 Gödel 逻辑编码物理知识约束训练，在合成网络、Tennessee Eastman 过程与两套模块化产线数据上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 「以正常行为先验重建不可观测变量、再据重建偏差判定异常」的设定，可能与「LVR 中视觉证据不完整时的内部状态补全与证据筛选」形成概念对应，但从过程故障诊断迁移到视觉推理是否可行仍需核查。
